Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:15: And in the Zohar (Parashat Tzav, page 31, beginning of side b), he explains "they defile him from above" as meaning that literally from above they flow impurity upon him, in these words: it is written, "sanctify yourselves and be holy" - whoever sanctifies himself from below, they sanctify him from above; whoever defiles himself from below, they defile him from above. "They sanctify him from above" is fitting, for the holiness of his Master rests upon him - but "they defile him," from where? And should you say, from above - does impurity rest above? Rabbi Chiya said, this is what we have learned: a deed below arouses a deed above - if the deed is in holiness, it arouses holiness above, which comes and rests upon him and he is sanctified through it; and if he is defiled below, he arouses a spirit of defilement above, which comes and rests upon him and he is defiled through it - for the matter depends on the deed, for you have no good or evil, holiness or defilement, that has no source and root above, and through the deed below, the deed above is aroused - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:16: And it is possible to explain it in a second way, close to the previous way in some respects, and I saw fit to elaborate on it because of the benefits that follow from it for the practice of holiness. "If a person sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him much" - in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5, and the Gate of Love, chapter 3, we explained two matters about this - but in order to connect the whole discourse, it appears that the intent is what they said, of blessed memory (Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 2), "one commandment draws another commandment," and so on - behold, at the start of the matter it is little, one commandment, and since the first draws the second, and the second the third, and the third the fourth, and so on without number, holiness multiplies - and therefore "they sanctify him much," for holinesses come to him from many commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:17: "If from below, they sanctify him from above" - all the pleasures of this world flow from the husks, there in the lower Asiyah, as explained in the Zohar - and behold, man is equal to a beast in the matter of eating, drinking, and marital relations, as they explained, of blessed memory, in Tractate Chagigah (16a): six things apply to human beings, three like the ministering angels and three like a beast - they walk upright, and speak the holy tongue, and have knowledge and understanding, like the ministering angels; and three like a beast - they eat and drink, and procreate, and excrete waste like a beast - to this point. And behold, man's walking upright, and likewise his excreting waste, are not within his control, for this is human nature from Adam, the first man, onward; but the matter of eating, drinking, and procreation, in which he is equal to a beast, he must sanctify, and not eat merely to fulfill his desire like a beast, and not be likened to the "spirit of the beast that goes downward to the earth," and similarly concerning procreation. He says that if he sanctifies himself from all the things that are below, like beasts soiled by the husks, as explained in Parashat Pekudei concerning the chambers of impurity, that in several ways they entice people with the pleasures of the world - they sanctify him above, meaning they say of him and proclaim in all the firmaments, so-and-so is holy, and no impure thing shall approach him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:18: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, page 225b), that wherever there is holiness, the husk does not touch, in these words: all those created beings of the world are all recognized above, whether from this side or the other side - those from the side of holiness are recognized above by Him, and the providence of that side is upon them; and those from the side of impurity are recognized by it, and its providence is always upon them. And in the place where that providence from the side of holiness rules, the other side does not gaze upon it, and never approaches it, and cannot push it from its place at all, in anything it does - and therefore (Psalms 34:16), "the eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous," and so on, because the Other Side cannot rule over him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:19: And further, "they sanctify him above" may also mean that when his soul ascends above every night, it ascends to a place of holiness, and the impure do not touch it - unlike other people, as explained at length in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 83a), on the verse (Isaiah 26:9), "my soul yearns for You in the night." And further, in Parashat Chayei Sarah (page 130a), in these words: come and see, this has been said: even in this world, when a person sleeps on his bed and souls need to roam the world and go out from the body, not every single soul ascends and roams to see the glory of the countenance of the Ancient of Days - rather, as it is always drawn, and according to its deeds, so its soul ascends. And if it is defiled - he sleeps and the soul goes out, and all those impure spirits strike it and cleave to it, in those lower levels that roam the world, and they inform it of matters soon to come into the world - and sometimes they inform it of false matters and mock it, and this has already been established. But if a person merits it, when he sleeps and his soul ascends, it goes and roams and breaks through among these impure spirits, and they all proclaim and say, clear the place, clear it, this one is not from our side - and it ascends among the holy ones, and they inform it of one true matter - to this point. And so he also explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 195b), that concerning this it is said (Psalms 24:3), "who shall ascend the mountain of the LORD, and who shall stand in His holy place" - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:20: And it is possible that concerning this aspect explained regarding "from below," he says in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 70b), in these words: Rabbi Yitzchak said, happy are the righteous in this world and the World to Come, for they are all holy - their body is holy, their nefesh is holy, their ru'ach is holy, their neshamah is holy of holies - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:21: And above this he spoke of the punishment of the wicked, who become harmers of the world, and afterward he says, happy are the righteous - and the reason is that all the evil of the wicked comes to them because of the impurity of their body in the desires of the world, but all the good of the righteous flows because of the holiness of their body, through which they merit a holy soul, and so on. But when the vessels of the body's limbs are blemished, even a holy soul does not rest in the body, for "anyone who has a blemish shall not approach." And through this discourse we can offer another interpretation of "if from below, they sanctify him from above" - that they flow into him a holy soul that comes from above him, from Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:22: "In this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come" - the meaning is that the holiness mentioned is the holiness of all the vessels of the limbs, and their purification from every kind of blemish, but he is occupied with his limbs in worldly matters and business dealings, in which there is no sin at all, and his thought spreads into the vessels of his limbs to see what they need from the world. But this holiness, which is the holiness of "this world," means that he sanctifies himself and separates from the affairs of this world as though he were not a member of this world - and this holiness depends on the holiness of thought and its cleaving always to what is above. How so? In the previous holiness, concerning eating, he separates from what is permitted-but-excessive and from pleasure, but intends the health of his body for the service of the Creator; but in [this] holiness, he intends, in eating, that he eats from the supernal table before the LORD, and his sustenance flows to him from the right - and there are several particulars to be explained concerning the matters of eating, and similarly for all the other particulars of worldly matters. And in his occupation with Torah and commandments, his thought is never for anything but to unify above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:23: It follows that such a person, although he is in this world, his thought is not in this world but in the World to Come. And therefore "they sanctify him for the World to Come" - for even in the World to Come he is holy, and his level shall not be like that of the rest of the people occupied with Torah and commandments without qualification, whose level is in the lower Garden of Eden - and these righteous ones are elevated above through the pillar in the middle of the garden, called "mikra'eha" [her convocations], as it is said (Isaiah 4:5), "and the LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion, and over her assemblies [mikra'eha], a cloud and smoke by day," and so on - and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel, page 219a) that this reality is said of the Garden of Eden, and the pillar is cloud, smoke, and brightness - cloud and smoke on the outside, brightness within - and he explains the reason why cloud and smoke are on the outside: so that the other righteous in the garden not gaze when these ascend above. And "her convocations" are the righteous who repaired their thought properly, as explained there (page 210b), that through the intention of Torah and prayer a garment is made for the soul, to raise it to the upper Garden of Eden - and it is called "her convocations," for they are called and summoned to adorn the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:24: And he says there, that when these souls ascend above for union, all the host of heaven open at that hour and say, happy are you, righteous ones, keepers of the Torah; happy are those who strive in Torah, for the joy of your Master is in you, for the crown of your Master is crowned through you - then, once light shines within light, two lights join together and shine, afterward they descend and gaze to delight in those souls of the righteous, and prepare them to be crowned above - and concerning this it is said (Isaiah 64:3), "the eye has not seen, O God, besides You, what He will do for him who waits for Him" - to this point. And what he says, "once light shines within light," is explained above this as the illumination of the direct light from the Righteous One [Yesod] and the returning light from the Shechinah, from the secret of the female waters from the righteous - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:25: It follows that the virtue of this holiness, the holiness of "this world," which is the holiness of thought, is greater than the previous - for the previous, even though one becomes holy above, as explained, he does not thereby merit to be of the band of "her convocations," as explained - but this one merits it. And the reason is that "with the measure a man measures, they measure him" (Sotah 8b) - a person who is in this world and separates himself from this world, whether in seclusion, in his speech, and all the other matters we shall explain in this Gate, with God's help, is found not to conduct himself in the manner of the people of this world; also in the World to Come, they sanctify him to be more separated and holy than the rest of the people of the World to Come who are in the Garden of Eden - and the intent is that he merits to be among the "people of the upper chamber" [bnei aliyah], of whom Rabbi Shimon said, "if there be a thousand, I and my son are among them, and if two, I and my son are they" (Sukkah 45b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:26: And along this path, his saying "in this world" is settled and precise - for the intent is that since this world is physical, it is a temporary dwelling for the soul, which is spiritual, for the soul has no bond or relation to this world - and the proof is that in the end it strips off the garment of this world. And therefore all his intent is toward the essential, spiritual World to Come that comes after this world, which is physical, ceasing and perishing - it follows that the term "this world" [olam hazeh] indicates two things: the first, that it is physical and perceptible, namely "zeh" [this], indicated by pointing a finger; and further, that it is not permanent, for after this [world] another will come. And therefore he should truly separate from the acquisitions and pleasures of the world, and from envy, hatred, and rivalry, and speak of worldly matters - for since he considers himself not a member of this world, he does not speak of it, and all his speech is in the occupation with Torah and commandments, which are from the supernal world, and likewise all his thoughts are in the supernal world, which is essential to the soul - for why should he trouble his thought with what will not benefit his soul, but on the contrary harm it? And therefore it is good for a person, at the time he is occupied with prayer or Torah, to think that he does not stand in this world but in the Garden of Eden before the Shechinah - and through this his thoughts are purified.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:27: And this introduction is a key to all the separation we shall explain in this Gate, and we mention it so as not to need to repeat things every time - for from the reason stated, he shall not look at what is unnecessary for him, shall not hear what would trouble him, shall not speak, and so on, and likewise in his eating and the other matters to be explained, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:28: Especially in the matter of eating, this is the greatest thing for subduing the husk in this world and the World to Come, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 141a): the bodies of the righteous, who delight in this world only in the pleasures of a commandment and the meals of Shabbatot, festivals, and appointed times, that impure spirit cannot rule over them, for they derive no pleasure of their own at all - to this point, and the rest of his words we copied in chapter 15. And this holiness is part of the holiness of "this world," among the general holinesses of this world, and it aids the holiness of the body in the World to Come, that a spirit of impurity not rule over it - because matter is flesh drawn from the husk, and since one diminishes his eating and derives no pleasure except from a meal of a commandment, the matter and the flesh itself is sanctified and no husk rules over it. And certainly he must also sanctify his other senses, such as speech, and other pleasures, such as the pleasure of sleep, marital relations, and the like - for this world is clothed in all these husks.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:29: And concerning those who sanctify themselves with this holiness, Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Parashat Terumah, page 151a), that there is no righteous person in the world who does not have the judgment of the grave, because of, and so on, except for those enduring pious ones of the world, who are fit to ascend to their Master with their souls to that supernal place fitting for them, and they are few in the world - to this point. And these are those righteous ones over whom the worm did not rule, because all their senses were properly sanctified, in such a way that the husk had no part in them - and this is the holiness of "this world," that while they are in this world they are [already] in the World to Come, as they said, "they are fit to ascend to their Master with their souls" - and therefore, in the World to Come, they rise in level above all the other righteous, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:30: And when you examine these three divisions we have explained, which are "harbeh" [much], "le-ma'alah" [above], "be-olam haba" [in the World to Come], you will find them corresponding to nefesh, ru'ach, neshamah - for the first holiness corresponds to the holiness of the commandments in Asiyah, corresponding to the nefesh, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 68b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:31: And "le-ma'alah" ["from above"] corresponds to the ru'ach, and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Vayikra, page 25a), in the discourse we copied above, when he comes to speak of a person's acquisition of nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah concerning the level of dreams - he says that when one merits the ru'ach and ascends above at night, "that ru'ach goes forth, breaking through mountains and cliffs, ascends and spreads and enters among the holy angels of the world," and so on. And he further says on, "then this is the bond of a person with holiness." And the intent of "breaking through mountains and cliffs" is the breaking of the husks called mountains and rocks, as it is written (1 Kings 19:11), "and behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind," and so on, "breaking the mountains and shattering the rocks in pieces" - and my teacher, peace be upon him, explained that "mountains" refers to Samael and "rocks" to Lilith.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:32: And he says, "then this is the bond of a person with holiness" - meaning, unlike one who has merited only the nefesh, who is not yet bound in holiness, as explained above this, "and that one who has not yet merited more than the nefesh, that nefesh needs to be repaired to receive the ru'ach; before it gains strength, it goes out, whatever goes out from that nefesh, and spreads in the world, and wishes to ascend, but cannot, until it encounters those of the air, and they inform it of matters, some near, some further off, and at that level it goes and is bound in his dream, until he acquires ru'ach; once he acquires ru'ach," and so on. And what he says, "those of the air," he explains above this as subtle husks that hang in the air. It follows that when he merits the ru'ach, which is through sanctifying himself below, as explained, then "they sanctify him from above," meaning he is bound in holiness and the husk has no part in him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:33: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Vayikra, page 25b) that through the occupation with Torah, a person merits the ru'ach and the neshamah, in these words: Rabbi Shimon said, happy are the masters of the soul, the masters of Torah, sons of the service of the holy King - woe to those wicked who do not merit to cleave to their Master, and do not merit Torah, for whoever does not merit Torah does not merit either ru'ach or neshamah, and their cleaving is to that side of evil weapons, and so on. And he was precise in his wording, saying "does not merit either ru'ach or neshamah," and did not say "does not merit nefesh" - for the nefesh is acquired through the occupation with the commandments, as explained in the Tikkunim, in the discourse we copied at the beginning of the chapter, that the positive commandments are in the secret of Asiyah, but the Torah's matter is through speech, and speech is from Yetzirah, as explained above, "from which the Chayot speak."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:34: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Bereshit, page 12b), the commandment to labor in Torah, that through the occupation with Torah a person merits the neshamah, in these words: the fifth commandment - it is written, "let the waters swarm abundantly with living souls" [sheretz nefesh chayah] - in this verse there are three commandments: one, to labor in Torah, and one, and so on... to labor in Torah and strive in it and increase it every day, and it should not be forgotten from him properly, as it is written "let the waters swarm" - this is the Torah, which one must strive in every day to repair his nefesh and ru'ach - for once a person occupies himself with Torah, he is repaired with another, holy soul, as it is written "sheretz nefesh chayah" - the nefesh of that holy chayah - for when a person does not occupy himself with Torah, he has no holy nefesh, and the supernal holiness does not rest upon him; but when he strives in Torah, through that toil he toils in, he merits that living soul and returns to be like the holy angels, as it is written (Psalms 103:20), "bless the LORD, His angels" - these are the ones occupied with Torah, called His angels on earth, and so on. And the end of the discourse's words: and therefore David said (Psalms 51:12), "create in me a pure heart, O God" - to labor in Torah - "and then renew a right spirit within me" - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that the merit of the holy soul, and even the ru'ach, all comes through the occupation with Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:35: And he explained, concerning the occupation with Torah, the conditions needed for one who wishes to merit the neshamah - one, his saying "to labor in Torah and strive in it," and he doubled his wording in saying "and strive in it," to allude that one must strive to grasp it within itself, in the depth of the matter he is occupied with, even in a halachah, as it is said (Proverbs 2:4), "if you seek it as silver, and search for it as for hidden treasures." And to this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, referred in saying, "let a person first study by rote and then analyze," as it is written (Psalms 119:20), "my soul is broken [garsah]," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:36: And he further says, "and increase it every day" - that he strive to be fruitful and multiply in it, just as one must be fruitful and multiply in the physical species, so must he be fruitful and multiply in the spiritual, and not have a sterile intellect that produces no fruit - and to this they referred in saying (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 13), "and one who does not increase decreases" - that a person should not learn today what he learned yesterday, ending up all his days occupied with one halachah, entering and leaving the study hall without any novel insight - and if, Heaven forfend, he does not add, so as to produce fruit, he is like a dry tree that produces no fruit, which they cut down, having no use except for the fire. And he says "every day," for just as the days are renewed, this day not being what it was yesterday - this is what we say (the Yotzer Or blessing), "and renews every day, continually, the work of creation" - so he must, every day, learn something new that he did not know before, and through this the days are found to shine and be repaired - meaning, the light of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:37: And he says, "and it should not be forgotten from him" - for one who learns and forgets is like one who gives birth and buries - and just as a person does not wish to bury his physical children, but that their existence endure in the world, so it must be with the matter of Torah - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 32b), that the death of children is because of the sin of neglecting Torah, as it is said (Hosea 4:6), "you have forgotten the Torah of your God; I will also forget your children." And therefore he must strive to teach something novel, namely to be fruitful and multiply, and strive to review everything he has, so as not to forget it - but one who learns and forgets is not given a novel insight, so that he not "bury" it the way he "buried" the previous.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:38: And when a person learns Torah in this manner, it indicates his great desire for Torah, and then the Holy One, blessed be He, flows into him a holy soul, and then he is like an angel stripped of matter. And the reason the acquisition of the soul is through Torah is that the source of the soul is above, from Binah, as it is said (Job 32:8), "and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding," and the Torah flows from there, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayetze) - and therefore the sustenance of the soul is through Torah. And so we find it called "bread," as it is said (Proverbs 9:5), "come, eat of my bread" - and he says in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, end of page 227a) that for this reason one must grind the words of Torah - for just as the body is nourished by physical bread after the wheat is ground, and the bran, chaff, and straw separated out, leaving fine flour, so, for the sustenance of the soul, one must grind the words of Torah - and we shall copy his words below, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:39: And so he says in the Tikkunim (page 49a), that the Torah gives strength and vigor to the neshamah, ru'ach, and nefesh, in these words: happy is he who unites neshamah and ru'ach with nefesh in the voice of Torah, which strengthens them - for whoever does not occupy himself with Torah, his neshamah, ru'ach, and nefesh weaken - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:40: Further, a reason for the acquisition of the neshamah through Torah is that Torah is acquired through forty-eight things (Avot, chapter 6) - "by attentive listening," and so on, "with awe," "with limited sleep," "with limited pleasure," "with limited conduct of the world" - for all these preparations are the distancing of love of the world from a person's heart. And the reason is that the Torah, because of its spirituality, rests upon a person until he acquires these traits in his heart, and distances himself from the good of loving this world, and strips off almost the garment of matter, to the point of resembling an angel in the refinement of his soul and body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:41: And it is possible to be precise here about the word "and the Torah is acquired [nikneit]" - which is not said this way of the priesthood or the kingship, for the wording of the beraita, as we have it, is "greater is Torah than the priesthood and than the kingship, for kingship is acquired with thirty virtues and the priesthood with twenty-four" - and it does not use the language of acquisition [kinyan] concerning them, but concerning Torah it mentions the language of acquisition. And the reason is that the Torah is called "the King's daughter," and behold, the law is that a woman is acquired in three ways, and acquisition is betrothal - so the reality of the Torah, called the King's daughter, and her betrothal, which a person gives her so that she be married to him, to reveal her secrets to him, is through the forty-eight things mentioned - and when a person merits the Torah by acquiring the things mentioned, then he merits the neshamah, and therefore Rashbi called the possessors of the soul "masters of Torah." In these words there, in Parashat Vayikra (page 25b): Rabbi Shimon said, happy are the masters of the soul, the masters of Torah, sons of the service of the holy King, and so on - and because a person merits Torah only through deed, he therefore says "sons of the service of the holy King."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:42: And whoever merits the neshamah is the one who merits to unify above, in the supernal sefirot, and his unification is a complete union - and so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 141b), of blessed memory, concerning the neshamah - and before this he explained the matter of nefesh and ru'ach - he says, the neshamah ascends immediately to its place, to the place from which it emerged, and this is that for whose sake the lamp shines to illumine above - to this point, relevant here. And because the supernal union is performed only through proper intentions, and the neshamah rests upon a person only through the acquisition of thought, therefore whoever has a neshamah is the one who unifies and causes the light of the Shechinah to shine through him above - but while a person is engaged with the affairs of matter, he has no neshamah, and his unification is no unification.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:43: And concerning the masters of the neshamah, it is said in the discourse before us, "if a person sanctifies himself in this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come" - and this is the world of thought, corresponding to the neshamah, as explained. And it is possible to say that "they sanctify him for the World to Come" means that they flow into him a soul of Atzilut - for whoever has a soul of Atzilut is holy for the World to Come, and this is the very matter explained above concerning those called "her convocations" - and it is impossible to attain that virtue except through sanctifying himself in meriting a soul of Atzilut, for whoever merits a soul of Atzilut has the highest of levels, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 24), in these words: happy are the righteous who have a supernal portion in the Holy One, blessed be He, a holy portion in the holinesses of the King, because they sanctify themselves with the holiness of their Master - and whoever sanctifies himself, the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies him, as it is written (Leviticus 11:44), "sanctify yourselves and be holy" - a person sanctifies himself from below, and they sanctify him from above; and when a person is sanctified with the holiness of his Master, they clothe him with a holy soul, the inheritance of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel, and then he inherits everything - and these are called sons of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God" - and this has already been established - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:44: And when you examine the words of this discourse, you will find that it mentions the three holinesses mentioned in the discourse of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, that we are occupied with - for he says, "whoever sanctifies himself, the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies him," corresponding to "if a person sanctifies himself a little," and so on; "if from below, they sanctify him from above" is explicitly mentioned, "a person sanctifies himself from below," and so on; corresponding to the third, he says "in this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come" - he was precise in saying "and when he is sanctified with the holiness of his Master" - and this is certainly the holiness of thought, in its separation from all worldly matters and its cleaving always to what is above, through his intention in the supernal attributes - and this is "the holiness of his Master" - then they clothe him with a soul of Atzilut, as explained, in such a way that through this he is holy in the World to Come, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:45: And he was precise in saying "they clothe him," and did not say "they give him a soul," and so on - along the lines of what was explained above, in chapter 2, concerning holiness, that in the matter of holiness there are two aspects: the first is the garment made for the soul from the drawing of holiness upon him, and the second is separation, as I elaborated there - and therefore he says "they clothe him." And along these lines I found in the Zohar (Parashat Chayei Sarah, page 125, beginning of side b), in these words: and therefore, whoever comes to purify himself is assisted from above, and the assistance of his Master surrounds him and guards him, and he is called holy - to this point. And from what he says, "surrounds him," it appears fitting to explain that it is like a garment that encircles a person from all around him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:46: And so it is also explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 245b), in these words: and he says that a cup requires rinsing on the outside and washing on the inside - and the secret of the matter, "and purify and sanctify" (Leviticus 16:19) - purity from within, holiness from without. And just as a cup's purity and holiness are not from within and without without water, so too the neshamah's purity and holiness are not without Torah - and therefore Rabban Gamliel said, whoever's inside is not like his outside shall not enter the study hall, because he is not from the Tree of Life but from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil - to this point. Behold, it is explained that holiness is from the outside. And incidentally we learn that a person's acquisition of purity and holiness is all through the occupation with Torah, and so it is also explained in Parashat Kedoshim (page 80b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:47: We find we learn that for a person to cleave to holiness, he should strive to merit nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, which are acquired through the performance of the commandments, the speech of Torah, the purity of thoughts, and the intention of Torah and the commandment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:48: And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (page 229a), he explains that these mentioned are also the three Names, Ehyeh, YHVH, Adonai, which add up to Yud-Bet-Kuf [numerically], and these three Names are the root for neshamah, ru'ach, and nefesh - whether in the secret of Atzilut, or below, in the throne, Chayah, and Ofan - namely, Ehyeh, which is the supernal Mother, nesting in the throne, in the three supernal sefirot; YHVH nesting in Metatron, in the six sefirot; Adonai, the Shechinah, nesting in the Ofan - see in the Tikkunim (page 23a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:49: And along these lines they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayera, page 99a) that for a person to draw holiness upon himself, it is through these three mentioned things, thought, speech, deed, in these words: Rabbi Abba opened (Psalms 24:3), "who shall ascend the mountain of the LORD, and who shall stand in His holy place?" Come and see, all the people of the world do not see on what the world stands, and the days go and ascend and stand before the Holy One, blessed be He - all those days that people stand in this world, for they were all created, and they all stand above - and from where do we know they were created? For it is written (Psalms 139:16), "days were formed." And when the days come to depart from this world, they all draw near before the supernal King - this is what is written (Genesis 47:29), "and the days of Israel drew near to die" - because when a person is in this world, he does not gaze or consider on what he stands, but every single day he thinks it is as though he goes about empty - for when the soul departs this world, it does not know to which path it ascends, for the path to ascend above, to the place where the illumination of supernal souls shines, is not given to all souls, for in the manner it was drawn after in this world, so is it drawn after it departs. Come and see, if a person is drawn after the Holy One, blessed be He, and his desire is after Him in this world, afterward, when it departs from him, it is drawn after Him, and they give it a path to ascend above, according to that drawing which was drawn in will every day in this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:50: Rabbi Abba said, one day I happened upon a certain city of the children of the East, and they told me from that wisdom they knew from ancient days, and we found books of their wisdom, and they brought me one book, and it was written in it that the will a person directs in this world thus draws a spirit upon him from above, in the manner of that will attached to it - if his will is directed to a supernal, holy matter, he draws that matter from above down to himself; and if his will is to cleave to the Other Side and direct himself to it, he draws that matter from above down to himself - and they said that the essence of the matter depends on words, deed, and will, to cleave, and through this that side to which he cleaves is drawn from above down. And I found in it all those deeds and services of the stars and constellations, and the matters needed for them, and how the will should be directed to them in order to draw them to themselves. Along these lines, all those spirits and demons of the impure side [assist] all those who wish to cleave to the impure side. Along these lines, whoever wishes to cleave above with the holy spirit - for the matter depends on deed, words, and the will of the heart to direct that matter, to draw it to himself from above downward and to cleave to that matter. And they said, just as a person is drawn from this world, so they draw him when he departs from this world, and in what he cleaves to in this world and is drawn after, so he cleaves in that world - if in holiness, in holiness; and if in impurity, in impurity. If in holiness, that side draws it to itself and it cleaves above, and becomes an appointed sun to [serve] the sun before the Holy One, blessed be He, among the other angels, in the manner it cleaved above, and stands among those holy ones, as it is written (Zechariah 3:7), "and I will give you access among those who stand here." Likewise, along these lines, if in impurity, that side draws it to itself, and it becomes like one of them, cleaving to them, and they are called "the harmers of people" - and at that hour they depart from this world, they take it and defile it in Gehinnom, in that place where they judge the impure people who defiled themselves and their spirits, and afterward it cleaves to them and becomes one of those harmers of the world. I said to them, my sons, this is close to the words of the Torah, and so on. And the conclusion of the matter: therefore a person must be drawn after the Holy One, blessed be He, and cleave to Him always, as it is written (Deuteronomy 10:20), "and to Him shall you cleave" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:51: Behold, it is explained that cleaving is acquired through deed, speech, and thought, and the reason is as explained, that these are the levels of the ascending ladder - and so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach, page 55b), in the explanation of the verse (Proverbs 27:10), "do not forsake your own friend, nor your father's friend" - which he explains there as the Holy One, blessed be He - precise in his words, that cleaving to Him, blessed be He, is through these mentioned things, and whoever does them does not forsake Him - and we shall copy that discourse below, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:52: And concerning these three things the Torah says (Deuteronomy 30:14), "but the word is very near to you, in your mouth, and in your heart, to do it" - "in your mouth" is speech, "in your heart" is thought, "to do it" is deed. And concerning these three it is said (Genesis 28:12), "and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and its top reaching to heaven," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:53: And incidentally, the virtue of cleaving to holiness is explained in the discourse, how great it is and how much a person is obligated to pursue it - as we said, that just as he cleaves in this world, so he cleaves in the World to Come.
